sources.locator: React Learn and Reference; React 19.2; provisions applicable to Dependencies and reactive values
sources.claim: Effect dependencies list every reactive value read so synchronization is reapplied when those values change.

canonicalExplanation.summary: The array after an effect lists the **reactive values** it reads: props, state, and anything computed from them during render. React re-runs the effect (cleaning up the old run first) whenever one of them changes, so the external system stays in sync. `[]` doesn't mean "run once and magically stay current"; it means "this effect reads **no** reactive values". If it actually reads some, it keeps using the **stale** values from the first render. Don't silence the lint rule; instead change the code so the effect needs fewer values, for example with an updater function or by moving an object inside the effect.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A study-group app connects to a chat room with an effect. The learner switches from the "Maths" room to "Physics", but messages still come from Maths. The effect was written with `[]` to "connect once". A chat connection effect depends on roomId and serverUrl because both determine the external connection. In this lesson you'll repair stale-closure and runaway-effect defects with correct dependencies.

```predict
{"question": "`useEffect(() => { const c = connect(serverUrl, roomId); return () => c.close(); }, []);` The roomId prop changes. What happens?", "options": ["It reconnects to the new room", "Nothing: with [], the effect keeps its first roomId"], "answer": 1, "why": "The effect never re-runs, so the connection stays on the old room. List roomId and serverUrl."}
```

examples.title: The study room that never switched
examples.situation: A chat connection effect depends on roomId and serverUrl because both determine the external connection.
walkthrough: **Stale closure:** with `[]`, the effect kept the first roomId, so switching rooms did nothing.
**Depends on roomId and serverUrl:** listing both makes React disconnect and reconnect when either changes.
**Test:** render with roomId "maths", re-render with "physics", and a test will assert disconnect was called once and connect with "physics".
examples.result: Switching rooms connects to the right room every time, and messages match the room on screen.

examples.title: The timer that stuck at 1
examples.situation: `useEffect(() => { const id = setInterval(() => setSeconds(seconds + 1), 1000); return () => clearInterval(id); }, []);` The timer shows 1 forever.
walkthrough: The interval's callback closed over seconds = 0 from the first render.
Fix: `setSeconds(s => s + 1)`, so the effect reads no reactive value and [] is honest.
examples.result: The timer counts 1, 2, 3... with the effect set up once.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: An empty dependency array makes any effect safe to run once with permanently current values.
misconceptions.correction: An empty array means the effect reads no reactive values. If it does read props or state, it keeps the values from its first render. List every reactive value, or rewrite so it truly needs none.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The timer that stuck at 1", which value was stale?

analogy.example: Dependencies are like **the settings a satnav watches**. If you tell it to watch nothing (`[]`), it keeps guiding you to the first destination even after you type a new one. Tell it to watch the destination (roomId) and it re-plans whenever that changes.
limitations: Satnavs don't re-plan on every glance; listing a new object each render makes the effect do exactly that.
Updaters are like "one more exit" instructions that don't need the full route.

steps.explanation: The chat connection effect runs with the first roomId.
React compares dependencies because roomId and serverUrl determine the external connection.
The old run is cleaned up and the effect re-runs for the new room.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing a dependency change. Step 1, Setup: connected to is maths; deps is ['maths', url]. The chat connection effect runs with the first roomId. Step 2, Change: deps is ['physics', url]; changed is roomId. React compares dependencies because roomId and serverUrl determine the external connection. Step 3, Resync: disconnect is maths; connected to is physics. The old run is cleaned up and the effect re-runs for the new room.

nearTransfer.prompt: An effect sets `` document.title = `${unread} new messages` `` with `[]`. The title never updates. Fix the dependencies and explain why.
expectedEvidence: The title updates when unread changes.

farTransfer.prompt: Find two effects in a project with suppressed lint warnings or suspicious [] arrays. Fix each by changing code (updaters, moving objects inside), and add tests that change props and check the external system follows.

remediation.explanation: Read the effect body and circle every prop, state value or render-computed value. **Each circle goes in the array.** If the list causes loops, change the code so fewer circles are needed.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The timer that stuck at 1".

recap.summary: To repair stale-closure and runaway-effect defects, list every reactive value the effect reads so React re-syncs when they change, remember [] means the effect reads none, and fix loops by creating objects inside the effect or using updater functions rather than silencing the lint rule.
